newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Wednesday:
Spokesman Thierry Daman said spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas would give a briefing on the results of the Commission's weekly meeting around 1630/1530 GMT.
He also said that there would be a technical briefing on landfil dumping of waste at 1600/1500 GMT if a decision was taken in Commission on this issue.

Daman said the group of Commissioners on public health would hold its first meeting after the Commission's weekly meeting. He said discussions would focus on BSE, labelling of genetically- modified organisms and cloning.
Daman said Thursday's Commission briefing would take place at 1145/1045 GMT instead of 1200/1100 GMT.

He also said Commissioner Padraig Flynn would hold a news conference at 1200/1100 GMT on Thursday on a Eurobarometer poll and the first Commission report on equal rights between men and women in view of international women's day.

Spokesman Peter Guilford said the Commission had approved the terms of the information technology agreement (ITA). He said it was a major step and that the deal was very promising. Guilford also said the Commission had asked the Council to approve the draft agreement by the end of the month. He said it would probably be on March 24.

Guilford said an agreement had been reached between the EU and the United States to eliminate all duties on brown and white spirits by the year 2000 instead of the year 2005 as stipulated in the Uruguay Round.
Spookesman Jochen Kubosch briefed on Thursday's Telecoms Council.
Spokesman Willy Helin said Commissioners Karel Van Miert and Padraig Flynn had met several times during the week to discuss the recent announcement of the closure of Renault's Vilvoorde plant.

Spokeswoman Barbara Nolan said a DGV preliminary examination showed serious questions to be answered by Renault with regard to information and consultation of the Vilvoorde workers. She said it seemed that these workers had been left with a 'fait accompli' and that the EU directives on collective redundancies and on the establishment of European Workers Council, transposed into national law, had not been respected in spirit.
The spokesman's services did not answer the question on the future Commission attitude following declarations by Belgian officials that they would boycott Renault products for public contracts.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/174: Commission adopts farm prices package for 1997/98.
- IP/97/177: Commissioner Fischler to lead on EU trade delegation to Japan.
- IP/97/178: Commission proposal on joint action for temporary protection of displaced persons.
- IP/97/179: ECU 80 million for industrial restructuring in the Netherlands.
- IP/97/180: The Commission supports industrial restructuring in Luxembourg.
- IP/97/182: Commission asks Council to approve ITA.
- IP/97/183: Commission adopts an action plan on satellite communications in the information society.
- IP/97/184: EU aid to support Romania's reform package.
- IP/97/185: Commission supports expedition to MN Derbyshire wreck in order to determine the cause of the accident.
- Memo/97/24: Renault: clarification of the situation regarding European law.
- Eurostat news release No 21/97: Harmonizing the way EU measures inflation.
- Oil bulletin No 858.
- ME97/5.3: Midday Express.
